fix: clang/lib/Sema/SemaRISCV.cpp:1450 'auto norm = ArgValue(*RoundArgNum);' -> 'auto norm = ArgValue(*NormArgNum);' (one token)
question: The one-token fix makes Sema enforce Round == 2^(Norm-1), the rule GAP9 GCC enforces and the fork's own comment states. Valid SDK calls (gap_mulsRN/gap_macsRN/gap_roundnorm with Norm=15, Round=1<<14) now compile, and out-of-range values are still rejected. But the two fork tests clang/test/CodeGen/RISCV/riscv-xpulpv2-intrinsics.c and riscv-xpulpv2-intrinsics-diag.c each contain 8 calls with Norm=2, Round=1 (machhsRN, machhuRN, mulhhsRN, mulhhuRN, mulsRN, muluRN, subRN, subuRN). GAP9 GCC rejects those inputs, and they passed only because of the bug. With the fix both tests FAIL: 'argument value 1 is outside the valid range [2, 2]'. In the -diag test the Sema error also stops compilation before the expected 'needs target feature' errors. Rule 2 forbids me to edit tests. Does the owner approve a recorded test exception (a test-regen task) that changes the Round argument from 1 to 2 in those 16 calls: intrinsics.c lines 332,350,440,467,494,521,548,584 and -diag.c lines 42,44,54,57,60,63,66,70? In intrinsics.c the matching '@llvm.riscv.pulp.*RN(..., i32 2, i32 1)' CHECK lines would change to 'i32 2, i32 2', regenerated with update_cc_test_checks.py. The Round operand is ignored by instruction selection (p.*RN encodes only Norm), so generated code is unchanged. The alternative is to keep the defect, and then the GAP9 SDK DSP kernels using *RN macros stay uncompilable.
